newsitem.title: GUINEA: West Africa foreign ministers discuss Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: West Africa foreign ministers discuss Sierra Leone.

text.p: West African foreign ministers met in Guinea on Thursday to discuss how best to restore democacy in neighbouring Sierra Leone following a May 25 military coup there.
Diplomats monitoring the meeting in the capital Conakry said that it was discussing the option of restoring ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah by force or negotiation.
One senior African diplomat following developments closely said before the meeting that the military option floated by regional power broker Nigeria did not have general regional support.
There was no consensus within the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) on that option and no resources available for the size of force needed, the diplomat added.
Ghana's deputy foreign minister said at the weekend that his country wanted to see a return to democracy via negotiation rather than force.

"Ghana still supports the OAU (Organisation of African Unity) decision reached in Harare recently, calling on all countries to do their utmost to restore the constitutional order in Sierra Leone," James Victor Gbeho told Reuters on Saturday.

"We believe that the best way to resolve the crisis is by diplomatic means, to reach a negotiated settlement, rather than by fighting," he added after talks with coup leader Johnny Paul Koroma and other military leaders.
Gbeho said the military government wanted a negotiated settlement to the crisis. "They are ready for talks," he said.
He declined to reveal the substance of his talks with Koroma, who was sworn in as head of state last week.

However, sources close to the talks said the coup leaders had discussed the idea of staying in power for only seven or eight months, rather than the two years they have announced, if an international peace-keeping force, other than the ECOMOG force already in the country, was deployed.

The West African ECOMOG force is led by Nigeria, whose gunboats bombarded Freetown on June 2 in a failed effort to reverse the coup. An anticipated further attack from the Nigerian troops has not so far come.
Koroma said on Wednesday in a speech marking the one month anniversary of the coup, that Tejan Kabbah could return home.

Earlier, a spokesman for the military leaders said they wanted an all-party conference bringing together Kabbah, the Kamajor traditional hunters who support him, the coup leaders and the Revolutionary United Front rebels who took up arms in 1991 and rallied to the coup.
